document_title: Port MacKenzie's $311 million line, and its unnamed ends

slides.headline:
A $311 million line.
Two ends.
No named data center.
The track is settled.
slides.body: The Alaska Railroad's board approved the $311 million line, 32 miles from Port MacKenzie to the main line near Houston. The Legislature backed it 58-1.

slides.headline:
$249 million federal.
$62 million local.
slides.body: AIDEA's share is $33 million in the Alaska Beacon's count and up to $34 million in the board's June resolution. The Mat-Su Borough adds cash, land and gravel. The railroad pays additional costs from savings.
labels: GROUND PROFILE ALONG THE LINE, VERTICAL x100

slides.headline:
Land for projects
nobody has named.
slides.body: DNR cut AIDEA's conveyance near Houston from 19,500 acres to about 6,800. AIDEA says uses could include an industrial hub or data centers. It says it hasn't identified a specific project.
labels: MORE THAN 2,300 COMMENTS, ALMOST ALL OPPOSED

slides.headline:
Proposed in 1992,
before there was a port.
labels: 2002 CLEARING BEGINS · 2007 STALLED · $180 MILLION SPENT, 2005 TO 2017

slides.headline:
Announced.
Not named.
slides.body: The Alaska Beacon reports a coal-fired computing data center has announced plans at the port. It doesn't name the developer. Terra Energy, a coal plant developer in a two-year marketing effort with the borough, isn't building one, Alaska Business reported in April.

slides.headline:
AIDEA's match goes
back on the table.
slides.body: AIDEA approved up to $34 million in June. Its board takes the match back up Friday, after the governor-elect asked AIDEA to freeze added spending until he takes office December 7th.

slides.headline: The cost has a source.
slides.body: The borough calls Point MacKenzie and parts of West Susitna more appropriate locations. Reconsideration requests on the Houston transfer are due November 30th.
labels: The data center has no name.

slides.headline:
What should a $311 million
public line be built to carry?

post_copy:
What is the $311 million Port MacKenzie rail line for if neither end has a named data center?

The Alaska Railroad's board gave the 32-mile line final approval last week. AIDEA says the Houston land could include an industrial hub or data centers, with no project identified. At the port the Alaska Beacon reports a coal-fired computing data center announced, developer unnamed.

Friday, November 27th, 10 a.m. AIDEA's match returns to its board.
November 30th. Requests to reconsider the Houston transfer are due.
December 4th. AIDEA meets again.
December 7th. The governor-elect who asked AIDEA to freeze added spending takes office.

Inside are the mapped route, who pays, both ends and the four dates.

Fund the line. Let the match wait for a name.

Is the $34 million ceiling AIDEA set in June a fair price before either end has a name?

#PortMacKenzie #AlaskaRailroad #MatSu

aftercare: Post before 10 a.m. Friday, November 27th, Alaska time. The caption's countdown opens on that meeting, so the first line goes stale once it resumes. Reply to every comment in the first 90 minutes. Note saves and comments after 48 hours.

When you reply, remember four things. Never name Terra as the port's data center developer, because the Beacon doesn't name one and Alaska Business said in April that Terra isn't building one. The amended second resolution's contents and dollar figure weren't fetched. The $33 million is the Beacon's count and up to $34 million is the June ceiling. The governor-elect's freeze request was general and didn't name the rail match.
editor_notes_for_email: The effort level in effect for this run was medium, not the high that settings.json sets. C13's coal-fired computing data center developer is unnamed by the Alaska Beacon, and Terra must not be named as that developer; Alaska Business (C49) says Terra isn't building a data center. The AIDEA Amended Second Resolution G26-07 (C33) was not fetched, so any changed figure in it is unknown and the deck says only that the agenda lists it. "AIDEA's match returns to its board" on November 27th rests on a chain: the November 19th agenda lists the item (C33), the schedule calls the November 24th meeting a continuation of November 19th (C31), and that meeting resumes November 27th (C30).
